33 Two resistors R1 and R2 are made from wire of the same material.
They are connected in parallel to each other in a circuit, as shown.

The diameter of R2 is half the diameter of R1.
The resistance of R2 is three times the resistance of R1.

hints: Notice $R_1$ and $R_2$ are in parallel, so compare the p.d. across them and use $R_2 = 3R_1$ to find the ratio of currents $I_1/I_2$.
Recall $I = nAvq$ with the same $n$ and $q$ for the same material, so $v_1/v_2 = (I_1/I_2)(A_2/A_1)$.
Convert the diameter statement to an area ratio: $A$ is proportional to $d^2$, and $d_2 = d_1/2$, then combine it with the current ratio.
walkthrough: Parallel branches have the same p.d. $V$. So $I_1 = V/R_1$ and $I_2 = V/R_2$.
Drift speed follows $I = nAvq$. Same material means same $n$ and charge $q$, so $v = I/(nAq)$ and $v_1/v_2 = (I_1/I_2) \times (A_2/A_1)$.
Substitute the ratios: $v_1/v_2 = 3 \times 1/4 = 3/4$. This is option B.

A.explanation: This inverts the area effect. $v$ is smaller in the larger area wire for a given current, so $A_2/A_1 = 1/4$ must multiply the current ratio, not divide it.

C.explanation: This uses diameter ratio $1/2$ directly as area ratio. Area depends on $d^2$, so $A_2/A_1 = 1/4$, giving $3 \times 1/4$ not $3 \times 1/2$.

D.explanation: This multiplies by $1/4$ twice. Only one factor of $A_2/A_1 = 1/4$ enters $v_1/v_2 = (I_1/I_2)(A_2/A_1)$.
